title: Trace filter correlation must pass experiment IDs to trace_info as integers, not str
answers: trace filter correlation fails on PostgreSQL with psycopg 3
trace correlation joint count error on postgres psycopg3
why does trace filter correlation break with string experiment ids
body:
Symptom: Trace filter correlation (the joint/filter1/filter2 counts comparing two trace filters) errors out or returns a failure on PostgreSQL with psycopg 3, while it works on SQLite.
Root cause: mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:calculate_trace_filter_correlation converted the validated experiment IDs back to str before they reached trace_info.experiment_id.in_(...) in _build_trace_filter_subquery and _get_trace_correlation_counts. psycopg v3 binds str as VARCHAR, which PostgreSQL will not compare to the INTEGER column.
Fix pattern: Keep IDs as int after _filter_experiment_ids (the public API still accepts strings, so coerce once at entry with int(e)), and type the helpers as list[int]. Do not add a str() round-trip back.
Constraints: Applies to every SQL filter that binds experiment IDs against trace_info.experiment_id (INTEGER). The same driver rule is in the numeric-search-filter note; this path had no coercion left to catch it. Regression test: tests/db/test_workspace_tracking_store.py:test_trace_filter_correlation_binds_integer_experiment_ids, which runs only against PostgreSQL with psycopg 3.
Applies: SQLAlchemy tracking store trace-correlation and trace-filter subquery code; any new trace query that filters on experiment_id.
applies: Trace correlation and trace filter queries in SqlAlchemyStore that bind experiment IDs against the INTEGER trace_info.experiment_id column.
says: Comparing two trace search filters crashes when using a PostgreSQL tracking database.
Trace filter correlation reports a database type error instead of showing matching counts.
Joint trace filter comparison fails on Postgres while working normally on SQLite.
Viewing correlation counts between trace filters results in an internal server error.
Fix trace comparison queries failing due to experiment identifier type mismatch on Postgres.
search: Trace filter correlation queries in SqlAlchemyStore must bind experiment IDs as integers when filtering against the INTEGER trace_info.experiment_id column. In mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:calculate_trace_filter_correlation, converting IDs to str caused psycopg v3 on PostgreSQL to bind VARCHAR parameters that fail comparison with INTEGER columns. Helpers _build_trace_filter_subquery and _get_trace_correlation_counts must take list[int] without round-tripping back to str, while public APIs still coerce incoming strings via int(e). This rule applies to all SQL filters matching trace_info.experiment_id and is tested by test_trace_filter_correlation_binds_integer_experiment_ids on PostgreSQL with psycopg 3.
